meta.title: Horn of plenty: why Scotland's national animal has never existed
meta.deck: Most countries choose an eagle, a lion or a bear as their emblem; Scotland settled on a beast from legend.
meta.note: 这是一篇仿《经济学人》风格的原创练习文章，不是真实外刊的转载。文中的事实是概括性描述，仅供语言学习，请不要当作引用来源。

sents.en: Horn of plenty: why Scotland's national animal has never existed
sents.zh: 丰饶之角：为什么苏格兰的国兽从来就不存在
notes: horn of plenty：丰饶之角，象征富足；这里双关独角兽的那只角。
national animal：国兽、国家象征动物。
has never existed：现在完成时，“从来不存在”。

sents.en: Most countries choose an eagle, a lion or a bear as their emblem; Scotland settled on a beast from legend.
sents.zh: 大多数国家选老鹰、狮子或熊作为国家象征；苏格兰却选定了一头传说中的神兽。
notes: emblem：象征、标志。
settle on：（考虑后）选定。
beast：野兽；a beast from legend：传说中的怪兽。

sents.en: Centuries later, it shows no inclination to trade it in for something more plausible.
sents.zh: 几百年过去了，苏格兰丝毫没有想把它换成一个更“靠谱”的动物的意思。
notes: show no inclination to do：毫无做……的意愿。
trade sth in for sth：用……换……（常指以旧换新）。
plausible：可信的、说得通的。

sents.en: Visitors to Edinburgh soon notice that the city is teeming with unicorns.
sents.zh: 来爱丁堡的游客很快就会发现，城里到处都是独角兽。
notes: Edinburgh：爱丁堡，苏格兰首府，读 /ˈedɪnbərə/。
be teeming with：充满、到处都是。
unicorn：独角兽。

sents.en: They rear up on fountains, perch on old market crosses and stare down from the gates of royal palaces.
sents.zh: 它们在喷泉上扬起前蹄，蹲踞在古老的集市十字碑顶上，从王宫大门上俯视众人。
notes: rear up：（马等）用后腿直立、扬起前蹄。
perch：栖息、高高地坐在……上。
market cross：集市十字碑，苏格兰老城镇的地标。stare down：往下盯着看。

sents.en: Gift shops, naturally, are crammed with plush versions sporting rainbow manes.
sents.zh: 礼品店里自然也塞满了顶着彩虹鬃毛的毛绒独角兽。
notes: naturally：插入语，“自然、当然”。
be crammed with：塞满了……。plush：毛绒的。
sporting：分词作定语，“戴着、顶着”。mane：鬃毛。

sents.en: Few tourists realise that the creature is not a whimsical marketing ploy but Scotland's official national animal.
sents.zh: 很少有游客意识到，这种动物不是什么异想天开的营销花招，而是苏格兰正式的国兽。
notes: not A but B：不是 A 而是 B。
whimsical：异想天开的、古怪有趣的。
ploy：花招、计策。

sents.en: Medieval Europeans took the unicorn rather more seriously than we do.
sents.zh: 中世纪的欧洲人对独角兽要认真得多。
notes: medieval：中世纪的。
take sth seriously：认真对待。
rather more ... than：比……要……得多，rather 加强语气。

sents.en: Bestiaries described it as fierce, proud and all but impossible to capture, an apt symbol for a small kingdom wary of its larger neighbour.
sents.zh: 动物寓言集把它描写成凶猛、高傲、几乎不可能被捕获的动物，正好象征一个对强大邻国处处提防的小王国。
notes: bestiary：（中世纪的）动物寓言集。
all but + 形容词：几乎……（不是“除了”）。
an apt symbol ...：同位语，补充说明。wary of：提防（已学）。

sents.en: Its horn was believed to neutralise poison, and so-called unicorn horns fetched extraordinary prices at royal courts.
sents.zh: 人们相信它的角能解毒，所谓的“独角兽角”在各国王室宫廷里能卖出惊人的高价。
notes: be believed to do：被认为……。
neutralise：使失效、中和。
so-called：所谓的。fetch a price：卖得（某价钱）。

sents.en: Most, it later emerged, were narwhal tusks hawked by enterprising traders from the far north.
sents.zh: 后来才知道，大部分其实是一角鲸的长牙，由来自遥远北方、头脑灵活的商人兜售。
notes: it later emerged：插入语，“后来才发现”。
narwhal：一角鲸。tusk：（象、鲸等的）长牙。
hawked by ...：过去分词短语修饰 tusks。hawk：兜售。enterprising：有进取心的、会做生意的。

sents.en: Scottish kings adopted the beast with enthusiasm, even minting gold coins known as unicorns.
sents.zh: 苏格兰国王们热情地采用了这头神兽，甚至铸造了名叫“独角兽”的金币。
notes: adopt：采用（已认识）。with enthusiasm：热情地。
minting ...：分词短语补充说明。mint：铸造（硬币）。
known as：被称作。

sents.en: When James VI of Scotland inherited the English throne in 1603, the royal coat of arms had to accommodate both nations.
sents.zh: 1603 年，苏格兰的詹姆斯六世继承了英格兰王位，王室纹章不得不同时容纳两个国家。
notes: James VI：读作 James the Sixth。
inherit the throne：继承王位。
coat of arms：纹章。accommodate：容纳、照顾到。

sents.en: England's lion and Scotland's unicorn were duly placed on either side of the shield, where they remain to this day.
sents.zh: 于是，英格兰的狮子和苏格兰的独角兽被分别放在盾牌两侧，一直保留到今天。
notes: duly：按照预期地、如期地。
on either side of：在……的两边。
where they remain to this day：非限制性定语从句；to this day：直到今天。

sents.en: In the version used north of the border, the unicorn takes pride of place.
sents.zh: 在苏格兰使用的版本里，独角兽占据了最显眼的位置。
notes: the version used ...：过去分词短语修饰 version。
north of the border：（英国人说法）边界以北，指苏格兰。
take pride of place：占据最重要、最显眼的位置。

sents.en: Look closely, however, and the unicorn is almost always bound in chains.
sents.zh: 可是仔细看，你会发现那只独角兽几乎总是被锁链捆着。
notes: 祈使句 + and：如果……就……（见语法点）。
however：插入语，表示转折。
be bound in chains：被锁链捆住（bind 的过去分词 bound）。

sents.en: Historians are divided over why.
sents.zh: 历史学家对其中的原因看法不一。
notes: be divided over：在……上意见分歧。
why 后面省略了 the unicorn is chained。

sents.en: Some argue that the chains signalled the might of a king who could tame even the wildest creature; others see a wry nod to how dangerous the animal was thought to be when left unchecked.
sents.zh: 有人认为，锁链显示了国王的威力，连最狂野的动物都能驯服；也有人把它看作一种带着幽默的暗示：人们认为这种动物一旦失去约束会有多危险。
notes: Some ...; others ...：有人……，有人……。
might：力量、威力（名词）。tame：驯服。
a wry nod to：带调侃意味地暗指……。left unchecked：无人约束时。

sents.en: An old nursery rhyme, in which the lion and the unicorn brawl over the crown, hints at a rivalry that has never quite subsided.
sents.zh: 有一首古老的童谣，讲狮子和独角兽为争夺王冠大打出手，暗示着一场从未真正平息的较量。
notes: nursery rhyme：童谣、儿歌。
in which ...：定语从句修饰 rhyme。brawl over：为……打架。
hint at：暗示（已学）。subside：平息、减弱。

sents.en: Today the unicorn has been co-opted by everyone from toymakers to tech investors, who use the word for start-ups valued at more than a billion dollars.
sents.zh: 如今，从玩具商到科技投资人，人人都把独角兽拿来为己所用；投资人用这个词指估值超过十亿美元的初创公司。
notes: co-opt：把……拿来为己所用。
everyone from A to B：从 A 到 B 的所有人（everything from 已学）。
start-up：初创公司。valued at：估值为……。

sents.en: Scots regard this craze with a certain amusement.
sents.zh: 苏格兰人看待这股热潮，多少带着点好笑。
notes: regard ... with ...：以……的态度看待。
craze：一时的狂热、热潮。
a certain：某种、一定程度的。

sents.en: Their unicorn, they point out, is not a sparkly pony but a belligerent beast with a horn like a lance.
sents.zh: 他们指出，他们的独角兽可不是亮晶晶的小马，而是一头好斗的猛兽，头上的角像一杆长矛。
notes: they point out：插入语。
sparkly：闪闪发亮的。pony：小马。
belligerent：好斗的。lance：（骑士用的）长矛。

sents.en: A nation that has spent centuries championing an animal nobody has ever seen can hardly be accused of lacking imagination.
sents.zh: 一个几百年来一直推崇一种谁也没见过的动物的国家，总不能说它缺乏想象力吧。
notes: 主干：A nation ... can hardly be accused of ...。
champion 作动词：拥护、捍卫。
can hardly：几乎不能。be accused of：被指责（已学）。

sents.en: And unlike eagles and bears, unicorns will never go extinct.
sents.zh: 而且和老鹰、熊不一样，独角兽永远不会灭绝。
notes: unlike：和……不同。
go extinct：灭绝。

vocab.note: 来自古希腊神话，是装满水果鲜花的羊角，象征富足，也叫 cornucopia。标题双关：独角兽那只角，加上苏格兰到处都是独角兽。

ex.en: The painting shows a goddess holding a [[horn of plenty]].
ex.zh: 这幅画画的是一位手持丰饶之角的女神。

ex.en: The harvest table was a real [[horn of plenty]].
ex.zh: 丰收的餐桌简直是一只丰饶之角。

vocab.def: a curved horn full of fruit and flowers, used as a symbol of having plenty of everything

vocab.note: 代表一个国家、组织的图案或事物：the national emblem（国徽、国家象征）。

ex.en: The maple leaf is Canada's national [[emblem]].
ex.zh: 枫叶是加拿大的国家象征。

ex.en: The team wears its [[emblem]] on every shirt.
ex.zh: 球队每件球衣上都印着队徽。

vocab.def: a design or object that represents a country, group or idea

cf.diff: symbol 最常用，可以是任何代表某种意思的东西（如 + 号）；emblem 多指国家、团体正式使用的标志图案。

ex.en: The dove is a [[symbol]] of peace.
ex.zh: 鸽子是和平的象征。

vocab.note: settle on / upon sth：经过考虑终于选定：We settled on a name for the baby.

ex.en: After hours of debate, they [[settled on]] Italian food.
ex.zh: 讨论了几个小时，他们终于决定吃意大利菜。

ex.en: Have you [[settled on]] a date for the wedding?
ex.zh: 婚礼日期定好了吗？

vocab.def: to choose something after thinking about it

vocab.note: show no inclination to do：毫无做……的意思；have an inclination to do：有做……的倾向。形容词 inclined（倾向于……的）。

ex.en: He showed no [[inclination]] to leave.
ex.zh: 他一点要走的意思都没有。

ex.en: My first [[inclination]] was to say no.
ex.zh: 我的第一反应是拒绝。

vocab.def: a feeling that you want to do something

vocab.note: trade sth in (for sth)：把旧东西交出去换新的，最常用于车、手机：trade in your old car。

ex.en: I [[traded in]] my old phone for a discount.
ex.zh: 我拿旧手机换了个折扣。

ex.en: We're going to [[trade it in]] for a bigger car.
ex.zh: 我们打算把它换成一辆更大的车。

vocab.def: to give something old as part of the payment for something new

vocab.note: 听起来合理、可能是真的：a plausible explanation（合理的解释）。反义 implausible。

ex.en: Her excuse sounded [[plausible]] enough.
ex.zh: 她的借口听起来还挺可信的。

ex.en: Is there a more [[plausible]] explanation?
ex.zh: 有没有更说得通的解释？

vocab.def: seeming likely to be true or reasonable

cf.diff: plausible 是“听起来可信、说得通”；feasible 是“能做到、可行的”：a feasible plan。

ex.en: Is the project financially [[feasible]]?
ex.zh: 这个项目在财务上可行吗？

vocab.note: 常用进行时 be teeming with：The river is teeming with fish.（河里到处是鱼。）

ex.en: The market was [[teeming with]] tourists.
ex.zh: 市场里挤满了游客。

ex.en: The pond [[teems with]] frogs in spring.
ex.zh: 春天池塘里到处是青蛙。

vocab.def: to be full of people, animals or things

cf.diff: swarm with 多指人或昆虫密密麻麻地乱动；teem with 更中性，常形容地方充满生物或东西。

ex.en: The kitchen was [[swarming with]] ants.
ex.zh: 厨房里爬满了蚂蚁。

vocab.note: 马受惊或发怒时抬起前腿直立；也比喻问题突然出现：Problems reared up.

ex.en: The horse [[reared up]] and threw its rider.
ex.zh: 马突然直立起来，把骑手摔了下去。

ex.en: A statue of a horse [[rearing up]] stands in the square.
ex.zh: 广场上有一座扬起前蹄的骏马雕像。

vocab.def: (of a horse) to rise up on its back legs

vocab.note: 鸟停在树枝上叫 perch；人或东西高高地放在边上也可以用：a house perched on a cliff。

ex.en: A crow [[perched]] on the fence.
ex.zh: 一只乌鸦落在篱笆上。

ex.en: She [[perched]] on the edge of the desk.
ex.zh: 她坐在桌子边上。

vocab.def: to sit on something high or narrow, like a bird on a branch

vocab.note: cram 是“硬塞”：cram clothes into a bag。be crammed with：（地方）挤满、塞满。

ex.en: The bus was [[crammed with]] schoolchildren.
ex.zh: 公交车里挤满了小学生。

ex.en: Her bag is always [[crammed with]] books.
ex.zh: 她的包里总是塞满了书。

vocab.def: completely full of people or things

vocab.note: plush toy：毛绒玩具。形容酒店、房间时是“豪华舒适的”：a plush hotel。

ex.en: The baby hugged a [[plush]] rabbit.
ex.zh: 宝宝抱着一只毛绒兔子。

ex.en: They stayed in a [[plush]] hotel by the lake.
ex.zh: 他们住在湖边一家豪华酒店。

vocab.def: made of soft, thick cloth; (of a place) expensive and comfortable

vocab.note: 作动词：sport a beard / a hat（留着胡子 / 戴着帽子），常有“显眼地、得意地展示”的意味。

ex.en: He turned up [[sporting]] a bright orange tie.
ex.zh: 他系着一条鲜橙色领带出现了。

ex.en: The singer [[sported]] silver boots.
ex.zh: 那位歌手穿着一双银色靴子。

vocab.def: to wear something in a way that makes people notice it

vocab.note: 马、狮子脖子上的长毛；也开玩笑地指人浓密的长发。

ex.en: The lion shook its golden [[mane]].
ex.zh: 狮子甩了甩金色的鬃毛。

ex.en: She brushed the pony's [[mane]].
ex.zh: 她给小马梳鬃毛。

vocab.def: the long hair on the neck of a horse or a lion

cf.diff: 同音词：mane /meɪn/ 是鬃毛；main /meɪn/ 是“主要的”。

ex.en: The [[main]] road is closed.
ex.zh: 主路封闭了。

vocab.zh: 异想天开的、古怪有趣的
vocab.note: 充满奇思妙想、俏皮古怪：a whimsical story（奇幻有趣的故事）。名词 whim（一时的念头）。

ex.en: The café has [[whimsical]] decorations.
ex.zh: 这家咖啡馆的装饰很奇趣。

ex.en: His drawings have a [[whimsical]] charm.
ex.zh: 他的画有一种奇思妙想的魅力。

vocab.def: playful and unusual, often in a way that is not serious

vocab.note: 为了得到好处而耍的小手段：a marketing ploy（营销噱头）。

ex.en: The free gift is just a [[ploy]] to get your email.
ex.zh: 免费礼物只是骗你邮箱的花招。

ex.en: Crying was her usual [[ploy]] to get sweets.
ex.zh: 哭是她要糖吃的惯用伎俩。

vocab.def: a clever plan or trick to get an advantage

cf.diff: ploy 是小花招、小手段；plot 是严重的秘密阴谋（plot 已学）。

ex.en: They uncovered a [[plot]] to rob the bank.
ex.zh: 他们破获了一起抢银行的阴谋。

vocab.note: 中世纪流行的书，描写各种真实或想象的动物，并附上道德寓意。

ex.en: The museum displays a beautiful medieval [[bestiary]].
ex.zh: 博物馆展出了一本精美的中世纪动物寓言集。

ex.en: Dragons appear in many old [[bestiaries]].
ex.zh: 很多古老的动物寓言集里都有龙。

vocab.def: a medieval book describing real and imaginary animals, often with a moral lesson

vocab.note: all but + 形容词 / 动词 = almost：all but impossible（几乎不可能）。注意不是“除了……都”。

ex.en: The town was [[all but]] empty.
ex.zh: 镇上几乎空无一人。

ex.en: By midnight, the party had [[all but]] ended.
ex.zh: 到午夜，派对差不多结束了。

vocab.def: almost; very nearly

vocab.note: an apt name / description（贴切的名字 / 描述）。也有“易于……”：apt to forget。

ex.en: It was an [[apt]] description of the city.
ex.zh: 这是对这座城市很贴切的描述。

ex.en: “Storm” is an [[apt]] name for such a wild dog.
ex.zh: 给这么野的狗起名“风暴”真贴切。

vocab.def: exactly right for a situation

vocab.note: 英式拼写 -ise，美式 neutralize。neutralise acid / a threat（中和酸 / 消除威胁）。来自 neutral（中性的）。

ex.en: Milk helps to [[neutralise]] the heat of chillies.
ex.zh: 牛奶有助于缓解辣椒的辣味。

ex.en: This powder can [[neutralise]] the acid.
ex.zh: 这种粉末能中和酸。

vocab.def: to stop something from having an effect

vocab.note: fetch a price：卖得某价钱：The painting fetched £2 million.。fetch 的本义“去拿来”大家熟悉。

ex.en: The old guitar [[fetched]] thousands at auction.
ex.zh: 那把旧吉他在拍卖会上卖了好几千。

ex.en: Fresh fish [[fetches]] a good price here.
ex.zh: 鲜鱼在这里能卖个好价钱。

vocab.def: to be sold for a particular amount of money

vocab.note: 生活在北极海域的鲸，雄性有一根螺旋状长牙，看起来就像独角兽的角。

ex.en: A [[narwhal]] can dive very deep.
ex.zh: 一角鲸能潜得很深。

ex.en: Some people call the [[narwhal]] the unicorn of the sea.
ex.zh: 有人管一角鲸叫“海中独角兽”。

vocab.def: an Arctic whale; the male has one long, twisted tooth

vocab.note: 从嘴里伸出来的长牙：elephant tusks（象牙）。

ex.en: Poachers kill elephants for their [[tusks]].
ex.zh: 偷猎者为了象牙杀害大象。

ex.en: The wild boar had sharp [[tusks]].
ex.zh: 那头野猪长着锋利的獠牙。

vocab.def: a very long, pointed tooth that grows out of an animal's mouth

cf.diff: horn 长在头上（牛角、独角兽的角）；tusk 是从嘴里长出来的牙。一角鲸那根“角”其实是 tusk。

ex.en: The goat has curved [[horns]].
ex.zh: 这只山羊长着弯弯的角。

vocab.note: hawk goods：到处叫卖。名词 hawker（小贩，新加坡的 hawker centre 就是小贩中心）。hawk 也是“鹰”。

ex.en: Men [[hawked]] fake watches outside the station.
ex.zh: 车站外有人兜售假手表。

ex.en: She spent the summer [[hawking]] ice cream on the beach.
ex.zh: 她整个夏天都在海滩上卖冰淇淋。

vocab.def: to try to sell things by going from place to place

vocab.zh: 有进取心的、会动脑筋做生意的
vocab.note: 敢想敢做、善于抓机会：an enterprising student（有进取心的学生）。名词 enterprise（企业；进取心）。

ex.en: An [[enterprising]] boy sold lemonade to the runners.
ex.zh: 一个机灵的男孩向跑步的人卖柠檬水。

ex.en: [[Enterprising]] locals rent out their spare rooms.
ex.zh: 精明的当地人把空房间租出去。

vocab.def: good at thinking of new ways to make money or do things

vocab.note: 名词 mint：造币厂；动词 mint coins：铸币。brand new 也可以说 in mint condition（崭新的）。

ex.en: The country [[minted]] a special coin for the Olympics.
ex.zh: 这个国家为奥运会铸造了一枚纪念币。

ex.en: Coins are no longer [[minted]] here.
ex.zh: 这里已经不再铸币了。

vocab.def: to make coins

vocab.note: 家族、城市或国家的盾形徽章，常有动物图案。复数 coats of arms。

ex.en: The city's [[coat of arms]] shows a golden ship.
ex.zh: 这座城市的纹章上是一艘金色的船。

ex.en: Old families often have their own [[coat of arms]].
ex.zh: 古老的家族常有自己的纹章。

vocab.def: a design in the shape of a shield used by a family, city or country

vocab.note: ① 容纳：The hall accommodates 500 people. ② 照顾到、迁就（需求）。注意拼写：两个 c，两个 m。

ex.en: The hotel can [[accommodate]] 200 guests.
ex.zh: 这家酒店能容纳 200 位客人。

ex.en: We'll try to [[accommodate]] your request.
ex.zh: 我们会尽量满足您的要求。

vocab.def: to have enough space for someone or something; to consider someone's needs

vocab.note: 按照预期或规定（发生）：The money was duly paid.（钱如期付了。）有“果然、照例”的意思。

ex.en: He promised to call, and he [[duly]] did.
ex.zh: 他答应会打电话，果然打了。

ex.en: The form was [[duly]] signed and returned.
ex.zh: 表格按要求签好交回了。

vocab.def: in the correct or expected way; at the expected time

cf.diff: 形近词：duly /ˈdjuːli/ 是“如期地、照例地”；dully 是“沉闷地、暗淡地”。

ex.en: The light glowed [[dully]].
ex.zh: 灯光暗淡地亮着。

vocab.zh: 边界以北（英国人指苏格兰）
vocab.note: 在英国，the border 常指英格兰和苏格兰之间的边界，north of the border 就是“在苏格兰”。

ex.en: Prices are a little lower [[north of the border]].
ex.zh: 苏格兰那边物价低一点。

ex.en: The law is different [[north of the border]].
ex.zh: 在苏格兰，法律不一样。

vocab.def: (in Britain) in Scotland, seen from England

vocab.note: take / have pride of place：被放在最重要、最显眼的位置：The trophy takes pride of place on the shelf.

ex.en: Her wedding photo takes [[pride of place]] on the wall.
ex.zh: 她的婚纱照挂在墙上最显眼的地方。

ex.en: The new car had [[pride of place]] at the show.
ex.zh: 这辆新车在展会上占据了最显要的位置。

vocab.def: the most important or noticeable position

vocab.note: be divided over / on sth：对某事意见不一：Experts are divided over the cause.

ex.en: The family was [[divided over]] where to go on holiday.
ex.zh: 家里人对去哪度假意见不一。

ex.en: Scientists remain [[divided over]] the question.
ex.zh: 科学家们在这个问题上仍有分歧。

vocab.def: having different opinions about something

vocab.note: 作名词：great power or strength：military might（军事力量）、with all my might（使出全身力气）。情态动词 might 大家都熟。

ex.en: She pushed the door with all her [[might]].
ex.zh: 她使出全身力气推门。

ex.en: The parade was a show of military [[might]].
ex.zh: 那次阅兵是军事力量的展示。

vocab.def: great power or strength

vocab.note: 表示觉得有点好笑，同时带点无奈或讽刺：a wry smile（苦笑）、wry humour（冷幽默）。

ex.en: He gave a [[wry]] smile when he lost again.
ex.zh: 他又输了，苦笑了一下。

ex.en: Her book is full of [[wry]] observations.
ex.zh: 她的书里满是带冷幽默的观察。

vocab.def: showing that you find something amusing in a slightly sad or ironic way

cf.diff: dry humour 是一本正经地说笑话；wry 更强调带点自嘲、无奈或讽刺。

ex.en: He has a very [[dry]] sense of humour.
ex.zh: 他的幽默感很冷。

vocab.note: a nod to sth：对……的暗示、致敬：The film's title is a nod to an old song.

ex.en: The design is a [[nod to]] the 1960s.
ex.zh: 这个设计是在向 60 年代致敬。

ex.en: His speech included a [[nod]] to his old teacher.
ex.zh: 他的讲话里提到了他的老师，算是致意。

vocab.def: a small sign that shows you know about something or respect it

vocab.zh: 不受约束的、未加控制的
vocab.note: go / be left unchecked：任其发展：If left unchecked, the disease will spread.

ex.en: If left [[unchecked]], the weeds will take over.
ex.zh: 要是不管，杂草会长满。

ex.en: Prices rose [[unchecked]] for years.
ex.zh: 物价多年来不受控制地上涨。

vocab.def: not controlled or stopped

vocab.note: nursery 是“托儿所”，rhyme 是“押韵的诗”。如 Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star。

ex.en: My grandmother taught me this [[nursery rhyme]].
ex.zh: 这首儿歌是我奶奶教我的。

ex.en: Many [[nursery rhymes]] have strange origins.
ex.zh: 很多童谣的来历都很奇怪。

vocab.def: a short traditional poem or song for young children

vocab.note: 在公共场合吵吵嚷嚷地打群架：a pub brawl（酒吧斗殴）。brawl over sth：为……打架。

ex.en: Fans [[brawled]] outside the stadium.
ex.zh: 球迷在体育场外打成一团。

ex.en: Two men were arrested after a [[brawl]] in a bar.
ex.zh: 两名男子在酒吧斗殴后被捕。

vocab.def: to fight in a noisy and rough way, usually in a public place

cf.diff: scuffle 是短暂的小推搡、小扭打；brawl 是吵闹、混乱的群殴。

ex.en: There was a brief [[scuffle]] at the door.
ex.zh: 门口发生了短暂的推搡。

vocab.note: 风暴、疼痛、怒气、洪水等慢慢减弱：The pain subsided.（疼痛减轻了。）

ex.en: We waited for the storm to [[subside]].
ex.zh: 我们等着暴风雨平息。

ex.en: Her anger slowly [[subsided]].
ex.zh: 她的怒气慢慢消了。

vocab.def: to become less strong or loud; to return to normal

cf.diff: 形近词：subside 是动词“平息”；subsidy 是名词“补贴”（已学）。

ex.en: Farmers receive a government [[subsidy]].
ex.zh: 农民领取政府补贴。

vocab.note: 把别人的东西、想法或符号拿来为自己服务：Brands often co-opt youth culture.（品牌常把青年文化拿来用。）

ex.en: The song was [[co-opted]] for a car advert.
ex.zh: 这首歌被拿去做了汽车广告。

ex.en: Politicians try to [[co-opt]] popular slogans.
ex.zh: 政客们总想把流行口号据为己用。

vocab.def: to use an idea or symbol for your own purposes

vocab.note: 某样东西突然流行、很快又过时：the latest craze（最新的热潮）。

ex.en: Every child wanted one during the yo-yo [[craze]].
ex.zh: 溜溜球热的时候，每个孩子都想要一个。

ex.en: The [[craze]] for bubble tea shows no sign of ending.
ex.zh: 奶茶热丝毫没有退潮的迹象。

vocab.def: something that suddenly becomes very popular for a short time

cf.diff: trend 是一般的发展趋势，可长可短；craze 强调突然、狂热又短暂。

ex.en: There is a growing [[trend]] towards working from home.
ex.zh: 在家办公的趋势越来越明显。

vocab.note: 很想吵架或打架的样子：a belligerent tone（挑衅的语气）。来自拉丁语“打仗”。

ex.en: The drunk man became [[belligerent]].
ex.zh: 那个醉汉变得很好斗。

ex.en: She replied in a [[belligerent]] tone.
ex.zh: 她用挑衅的语气回答。

vocab.def: unfriendly and wanting to argue or fight

cf.diff: aggressive 很常用，还可以是褒义（积极进取：aggressive marketing）；belligerent 更正式，只表示敌意、想打架。

ex.en: Some dogs are [[aggressive]] towards strangers.
ex.zh: 有些狗对陌生人很凶。

vocab.note: 中世纪骑士骑马冲刺时用的长矛。

ex.en: The knight lowered his [[lance]] and charged.
ex.zh: 骑士放低长矛，冲了过去。

ex.en: The museum has a row of old [[lances]].
ex.zh: 博物馆里有一排古老的长矛。

vocab.def: a long spear used by soldiers on horses in the past

vocab.note: 作动词：大力支持、为……奔走：champion women's rights（捍卫女性权利）。名词“冠军”大家都熟。

ex.en: She has [[championed]] cycling in the city for years.
ex.zh: 她多年来一直在城里推广骑自行车。

ex.en: The paper [[champions]] local businesses.
ex.zh: 这家报纸力挺本地商家。

vocab.def: to publicly support a person, idea or cause

vocab.note: extinct：灭绝的。go / become extinct：灭绝。名词 extinction。

ex.en: The dodo [[went extinct]] long ago.
ex.zh: 渡渡鸟很久以前就灭绝了。

ex.en: Many frogs could [[go extinct]] this century.
ex.zh: 许多青蛙可能在本世纪灭绝。

vocab.def: to stop existing as a species

vocab.note: 祈使句后面接 and + 结果，表示条件：“只要……就……”。Look closely and you'll see ... = If you look closely, you'll see ...。如果接 or，就是“否则”：Hurry, or you'll be late.

ex.en: Work hard [[and]] you will pass.
ex.zh: 只要努力，你就能通过。

ex.en: Turn left at the church [[and]] you'll see the station.
ex.zh: 在教堂那儿左转，就能看到车站。

vocab.conn: 祈使句, + and + 结果（= If you ..., ...）；祈使句, + or + 结果（= 否则）
vocab.say: Look closely, and you will see.

pick.q: Press this button ___ the door will open.
pick.why: 按按钮的结果是门会开，表示“只要……就……”，用 and。

pick.q: Hurry up, ___ you'll miss the bus.
pick.why: “快点，否则赶不上车”，表示“否则”，用 or。

cloze.hint: 最显要的位置（___ of place）
拿来为己所用（过去分词）
仔细看就会发现（Look closely, however, ___）

breakdown.en: Some argue that the chains signalled the might of a king who could tame even the wildest creature; others see a wry nod to how dangerous the animal was thought to be when left unchecked.
points: 分号把两半连起来：Some argue that ... ; others see ... —— 有人认为……；也有人看作……。
前半：the might of a king who could tame even the wildest creature，who 引导定语从句修饰 king；might 是名词“威力”。
后半：a wry nod to + 宾语从句 how dangerous the animal was thought to be，“暗指这种动物被认为有多危险”。
when left unchecked = when it was left unchecked，省略了主语和 be 动词。
